title: The affine derived coherator has invertible comparison unit and counit
statement: Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and write $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal O_T)$ for quasi-coherent module sheaves [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-derived-category]. Let $I_T:D(\mathcal A_T)\to D(\mathcal O_T)$ and $C_T=Rq_T:D(\mathcal O_T)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the termwise inclusion and derived coherator with adjunction, unit $e_T$ and counit $d_T$ of [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-coherator-adjunction]. For every $B\in D(\mathcal A_T)$ the unit $e_T(B):B\to C_TI_TB$ is an isomorphism. For every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ the counit $d_T(E):I_TC_TE\to E$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08D9, perfect-lemma-affine-coherator (3), with its induced adjunction; the identification by derived global sections is in (1)--(2).

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $S:\operatorname{Mod}_A\to\mathcal A_T$ be associated sheaf and $G=\Gamma(T,-)|_{\mathcal A_T}$. The affine tilde/global-sections node, clauses (2) and (3), gives natural isomorphisms $\mathrm{id}\cong GS$ and $SG\cong\mathrm{id}$, hence an additive equivalence. Both categories are abelian, using the quasi-coherent Grothendieck node for $\mathcal A_T$. Both functors are exact: transport a kernel (respectively cokernel) diagram across the Hom bijections of this equivalence; its universal factorization property remains the kernel (respectively cokernel) property. Thus they preserve kernels and cokernels, and hence short exact sequences. This uses the quasi-coherent category, not all module sheaves, for $G$.

Apply exact-functor derived factorization to $S$ and $G$, obtaining termwise functors $S_D:D(A)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ and $G_D:D(\mathcal A_T)\to D(A)$. On complexes the two ordinary natural isomorphisms of Step 1 give $G_DS_D\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $S_DG_D\cong\mathrm{id}$ after localization: precisely, clause (2) of the localization universal-property node lifts each termwise isomorphism, and compatibility with compositions lifts its inverse as an inverse. Thus $S_D$ and $G_D$ are quasi-inverse on unbounded derived categories. No resolution or boundedness restriction enters this construction.

source.place: Tag 015F, derived-lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; natural transformations through localization as in the cited localization node

proof.text: The inclusion $i_T$ is exact by the quasi-coherent Grothendieck node. For a complex $B$, $H^n(i_TB)=i_T H^n(B)$ by preservation of kernels and cokernels, so $I_T$ lands in the full category $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$. Let $F:D(A)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ be the equivalence of the affine derived-equivalence node. Its composite with the full inclusion, and $I_TS_D$, both apply associated sheaf termwise on complexes. Clause (2) of the localization node therefore supplies a natural isomorphism between these functors; it also lies in the full quasi-coherent subcategory. Consequently the corestriction of $I_T$ is naturally isomorphic to $FG_D$, an equivalence by Step 2. In particular $I_T$ is fully faithful into $D(\mathcal O_T)$, and every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ admits an isomorphism $v:I_TB\xrightarrow{\sim}E$.

Use the specified adjunction $I_T\dashv C_T$ of the scheme-derived-coherator node. Since $I_T$ is fully faithful by Step 3, the fully faithful left-adjoint unit lemma gives that its actual unit $e_T(B):B\to C_TI_TB$ is invertible for every $B$. This conclusion is about the specified adjunction, so no choice of a different equivalence unit is involved.

source.place: Tag 08D9, perfect-lemma-affine-coherator (3), induced adjunction; abstract unit criterion as cited

proof.text: For $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ choose $v:I_TB\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ from Step 3. The triangle identity of the specified adjunction is $d_T(I_TB)\circ I_T(e_T(B))=1_{I_TB}$. Step 4 makes the second factor invertible, so $d_T(I_TB)=I_T(e_T(B))^{-1}$. Counit naturality gives $d_T(E)\circ I_TC_T(v)=v\circ d_T(I_TB)$, hence $d_T(E)=v\circ d_T(I_TB)\circ I_TC_T(v)^{-1}$. All factors are invertible. This proves the counit assertion for the actual $d_T$, including arbitrary unbounded $E$; none of the cited affine results assumes Noetherianity.
